criterion_results.unevaluated: Scaffold-only. The harness writes this value and submission rejects it.
criterion_results.pending_harness: Only for shell criteria in the resolved invocation rubric, which the harness executes. Eligibility validation precedes gates. The task record's evaluation.deterministic settles the attempt; evaluation.self and stage history self_criteria preserve worker claims. A missing result or unauthorized skip cannot settle a pending check. An explicitly disabled gate retains its disabled record.
criterion_results.skipped: Terminal non-success. Permitted on a blocked output or on a shell criterion when the stage already failed. Forbidden on success.
criterion_results.not_applicable: Worker judgment that a criterion does not apply. Hard criteria MUST NOT use it.

how the criterion is proven: test (a gate lane), review (reading the code), live (a browser or app check QA runs), or observe (a signal after ship). A criterion that changes a browser or app surface is live; one that needs an operator's live observation or a production signal is observe; prefer test when a gate lane can prove it; use review for structure, wording, and docs

{ path, contract }: path is '<test file path>' optionally followed by '::<test case>' (pytest node ids and the spaced ' :: ' display form both resolve) and the file portion must exist, e.g. 'tests/unit/example.test.ts::adds provenance rows'; contract is one non-empty sentence naming the behavior the test proves. Every new test file and every changed test file with a net-positive test(/it( count MUST have an entry with a contract. A bare string still parses as { path } and fails only when that delta requires a contract. A change that adds no tests needs no entry.
